note: The lupines, pinks (Dianthus), blanket flowers (Gaillardia) and Baptisia choices of 0.9.163. Sizes are the source's figures; heightIn is the plant in flower near the middle of the range, and each drawing was solved to stand at it (within 6%). Where two sources differ the estimate says which was used. MBG gives no zones for some hybrids; Walters' perennials.com then supplies them.

sources.mbg: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder, https://plantfinder.mobot.org/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=<id>, read 2026-11-24
sources.wildflower: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center, https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=<symbol>, read 2026-11-24
sources.kpu: Kwantlen Polytechnic University plant database, https://plantdatabase.kpu.ca/PlantPrint/dipl, read 2026-11-24

wildlupine.estimates: Wildflower Center: up to about 2 ft, blue/purple (rarely pink or white), Apr-Jul, dry sandy soils, NH to s. Ont., n. IL, n. IN and e. MN, south to FL and LA. Prairie Moon: 2 ft, zones 3-8, May-July, spacing 10-18 in (used for spread), sand, may take a few years to bloom, Karner blue larval host. It goes dormant by late summer, so no Fall seed or Winter leaves are drawn.

bigleaflupine.estimates: Wildflower Center: 3-5 ft, blue, purple or reddish, May; streambanks and meadows, Coast Ranges CA to AK, east to AB and CO; 'widely naturalized and often invasive in northeastern US and eastern Canada'. No zones given; 4-8 follows Walters' Mini Gallery (from L. polyphyllus) and the Russell hybrids' MBG range. Spread an estimate.

russelllupine|masterpiece.estimates: Walters 27-29 in x 18-23 in, magenta-purple with an orange fleck.

russelllupine|gladiator.estimates: Walters 25-29 in x 21-25 in, orange and yellow.
